<align="center">At a time when frogs had no need to croak in the dark night,</align>
<align="center">their chorus wasn't as noisy as it is today,</align>
<align="center">and reeds had just sprouted in the marshland back then.</align>
<align="center">Before tiny fish, mealworms, and shrimp came to be,</align>
<align="center">the frogs would fish in the crystal-clear gulf current,</align>
<align="center">paddling their canoes tirelessly day and night.</align>
<align="center">Beautiful sailfish, swordfish, and of course, tuna,</align>
<align="center">all slowly fermented under the sun,</align>
<align="center">turning into the most exquisite soup stock.</align>
<align="center"> </align>
<align="center">One day, the frogs became puzzled:</align>
<align="center">With so much food in the world,</align>
<align="center">why must they eat the dried meat passed down from their great-grandparents?</align>
<align="center">They sank their offerings into the mud,</align>
<align="center">and wished upon the sacred tree in the marsh for new delicious food.</align>
<align="center">Food that would melt in their mouths,</align>
<align="center">food that would be absolutely fresh.</align>
<align="center">So the sacred tree smoothed the earth's head,</align>
<align="center">using starlight reflected in rippling water like hair,</align>
<align="center">to create tiny fish, mealworms, and shrimp.</align>
<align="center"> </align>
<align="center">Time passed this way,</align>
<align="center">as the fast-paced frogs lived happily each day.</align>
<align="center">But they grew more accustomed to the mud,</align>
<align="center">ambushing prey in the darkness,</align>
<align="center">croaking in crowds on spring nights,</align>
<align="center">and scorned with mocking glances,</align>
<align="center">even by their own kind.</align>
